profile.bio: Introduce your practice — the subjects you keep returning to, and what a wall of your work should feel like. The paintings in this starter are museum Open Access samples and cannot be published as your work.

blocks.text: A quieter room — portraits and figures, two to a row.

01-blue-morning.jpg.title: Blue Morning
01-blue-morning.jpg.alt: From under an elevated train track, we look at a cluster of people hammering and working on the far side of a wooden fence, all against a silvery-blue building that fills most of the background in this horizontal painting.
01-blue-morning.jpg.description: George Bellows. Blue Morning, 1909. National Gallery of Art.

02-the-lone-tenement.jpg.title: The Lone Tenement
02-the-lone-tenement.jpg.alt: A six-story, narrow building stands alone in an otherwise unoccupied lot under the deck of a high bridge, with a river and cityscape in the background in this horizontal painting.
02-the-lone-tenement.jpg.description: George Bellows. The Lone Tenement, 1909. National Gallery of Art.

03-anne-with-a-japanese-parasol.jpg.title: Anne with a Japanese Parasol
03-anne-with-a-japanese-parasol.jpg.alt: This painting shows a young girl standing and facing forward.
03-anne-with-a-japanese-parasol.jpg.description: George Bellows. Anne with a Japanese Parasol, 1917. National Gallery of Art.

04-new-york.jpg.title: New York
04-new-york.jpg.alt: We look slightly down onto a crush of pedestrians, horse-drawn carriages, wagons, and streetcars enclosed by a row of densely spaced buildings and skyscrapers opposite us in this horizontal painting.
04-new-york.jpg.description: George Bellows. New York, 1911. National Gallery of Art.

05-nude-with-red-hair.jpg.title: Nude with Red Hair
05-nude-with-red-hair.jpg.alt: Shown from the knees up, a woman sits partially covered by a black cloth as she holds one forearm across her bare breasts in this vertical painting.
05-nude-with-red-hair.jpg.description: George Bellows. Nude with Red Hair, 1920. National Gallery of Art.

01-chester-dale.jpg.title: Chester Dale
01-chester-dale.jpg.alt: This painting shows a man from the waist up, his body turned slightly to the right.
01-chester-dale.jpg.description: George Bellows. Chester Dale, 1922. National Gallery of Art.

02-florence-sittenham-davey-mrs-randall-.title: Florence Sittenham Davey (Mrs. Randall Davey)
02-florence-sittenham-davey-mrs-randall-.alt: This painting is a portrait of a seated woman shown from the knees upwards.
02-florence-sittenham-davey-mrs-randall-.description: George Bellows. Florence Sittenham Davey (Mrs. Randall Davey), 1914. National Gallery of Art.

03-little-girl-in-white-queenie-burnett..title: Little Girl in White (Queenie Burnett)
03-little-girl-in-white-queenie-burnett..alt: A young, pale-skinned girl wearing a white dress stands against a darkened background in this vertical portrait painting.
03-little-girl-in-white-queenie-burnett..description: George Bellows. Little Girl in White (Queenie Burnett), 1907. National Gallery of Art.

04-maud-murray-dale-mrs-chester-dale.jpg.title: Maud Murray Dale (Mrs. Chester Dale)
04-maud-murray-dale-mrs-chester-dale.jpg.alt: This painting shows a seated woman from the waist up.
04-maud-murray-dale-mrs-chester-dale.jpg.description: George Bellows. Maud Murray Dale (Mrs. Chester Dale), 1919. National Gallery of Art.

05-my-family.jpg.title: My Family
05-my-family.jpg.alt: This painting shows an adult woman and two children on a white lounge chair.
05-my-family.jpg.description: George Bellows. My Family, 1916. National Gallery of Art.
